Header.CaseTitle: Sharma v Meridian Financial Services Ltd

Counsel.Lead: William Hughes KC; William Anderson (instructed by Allen & Overy LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant claims she was subjected to race discrimination and harassment during her employment and that her subsequent dismissal constituted victimisation for having raised complaints about discriminatory treatment.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant was employed as a Senior Analyst from September 2019 until her dismissal in March 2024.
Throughout her employment, the Appellant was subjected to microaggressions and exclusion from team events by her manager.
The Appellant raised a formal grievance alleging race discrimination in November 2023.
Two months after raising her grievance, the Appellant was placed on a Performance Improvement Plan.
The Appellant was dismissed in March 2024 allegedly for failing the PIP.

Contentions.item: The Appellant was treated less favourably than comparators because of her race.
The conduct of her manager constituted harassment related to race.
The timing of the PIP and dismissal demonstrates victimisation.
The burden shifts to the Respondent to prove non-discriminatory reasons.

AuthoritiesCited.Authority: Shamoon v Chief Constable of the Royal Ulster Constabulary [2003] UKHL 11
Igen Ltd v Wong [2005] EWCA Civ 142
Nagarajan v London Regional Transport [1999] IRLR 572
